newsitem.title: GERMANY: BUBA'S KUEHBACHER SEES DIRE RESULTS IF EMU FAILS.
newsitem.headline: BUBA'S KUEHBACHER SEES DIRE RESULTS IF EMU FAILS.

text.p: A collapse of Europe's planned currency union would be disastrous and have particularly devastating consequences for Germany, Bundesbank council member Klaus-Dieter Kuebacher warned on Thursday.
"If the European currency union does not happen it would signal a step backwards in the process of European integration leading to a return of individual economic policies," he said.
"Especially for Germany this would have devastating consequences," said Kuehbacher, who is also president of the regional central bank of Berlin and Brandenburg.
In a speech prepared for delivery in Stendal and made available here, Kuehbacher said Germany's export-oriented industries would benefit from the currency union.
Since Germany has few natural resources it is particularly dependent on stable currency rates to secure jobs, the official said.

The Maastricht Treaty on European Economic and Monetary Union states the currency union will be launched on January 1, 1999 and Kuehbacher said as long as the European Commission does not alter the date, the timetable must be maintained.

But Kuehbacher, who had earlier said Italy should not take part in the union from the beginning as it failed to meet fiscal entry requirements, declined to speculate on which nations may be among the first group to adopt the new currency.
"It is still too early for speculation" on that topic, Kuehbacher said.
Even before the launch, Kuehbacher said much political action was needed to convince citizens that the currency union is important and for them to accept it.
